questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): PCR can detect a bacterial or viral infection even before the symptoms of the disease become visible.
Reason (R): PCR amplifies the nucleic acid of the pathogen, so even a very low concentration of the pathogen becomes detectable.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that a very low concentration of bacteria or virus can be detected at a time when symptoms are not yet visible.
R is true. This is possible because PCR amplifies the pathogen's nucleic acid to detectable amounts.
Amplification is exactly what allows such early detection, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Pomato, obtained by somatic hybridisation of tomato and potato protoplasts, did not have all the desired characteristics for commercial use.
In Eli Lilly's method, pro-insulin containing the C peptide was expressed in E. coli, and the C peptide was then removed to give mature insulin.
PCR can detect a pathogen at very low concentration, even before disease symptoms appear, by amplifying its nucleic acid.
Over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: pomato was produced, but it lacked the full combination of traits needed for commercial use.
(2) Incorrect: Eli Lilly (1983) prepared two separate DNA sequences for chains A and B and expressed them in E. coli plasmids. The chains were extracted separately and joined by disulphide bonds. No pro-insulin or C peptide step was involved.
(3) Correct: PCR amplification lets very low pathogen levels be detected, as in HIV testing.
(4) Correct: NCERT states that over 95% of transgenic animals are mice.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: NCERT mentions cystic fibrosis in the context of transgenic animals under two different categories of use. Which pair of categories is it?
options: Study of normal physiology and vaccine safety
Study of disease and biological products
Biological products and chemical safety testing
Vaccine safety and chemical safety testing
questions.explanation:
Under study of disease, cystic fibrosis is listed among the human diseases for which transgenic models exist.
Under biological products, NCERT says attempts are being made to produce treatments for PKU and cystic fibrosis, similar to $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin for emphysema.
Neither vaccine safety, which concerns polio, nor chemical toxicity testing mentions cystic fibrosis.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are benefits of genetic modification of crop plants as described in NCERT?
(i) Greater tolerance to cold, drought, salt and heat
(ii) Reduced post-harvest losses
(iii) Enhanced nutritional value, as in golden rice
(iv) Increased efficiency of mineral usage by plants
(v) Increased reliance on chemical pesticides
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: GM crops tolerate abiotic stresses better.
(ii) Correct: GM has helped reduce post-harvest losses.
(iii) Correct: Golden rice is enriched with vitamin A.
(iv) Correct: Better mineral usage prevents early exhaustion of soil fertility.
(v) Incorrect: Pest-resistant GM crops reduce, not increase, reliance on chemical pesticides.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about Bt cotton is INCORRECT?
options: It reduces the need for chemical insecticides because the plant itself produces an insecticidal protein
The toxin kills the pest by forming pores in midgut epithelial cells, causing swelling and lysis
The toxin present in the plant tissue is already active and kills insects on contact with their body surface
Proteins encoded by cryIAc and cryIIAb are used to protect it from bollworms
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Bt cotton acts as a bio-pesticide and reduces reliance on insecticide sprays.
(2) Correct: The activated toxin makes pores in midgut cells, which swell and lyse.
(3) Incorrect: The toxin is an inactive protoxin. It must be ingested and activated by alkaline gut pH, so it does not act by surface contact.
(4) Correct: NCERT names cryIAc and cryIIAb for controlling cotton bollworms.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Rosie are correct?
(i) Rosie was produced in 1997.
(ii) Her milk contained the human protein at 2.4 grams per litre.
(iii) The human protein in her milk was $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin.
(iv) Her milk was nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow milk.
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Rosie, the first transgenic cow, was produced in 1997.
(ii) Correct: her milk was enriched with the human protein at 2.4 g per litre.
(iii) Incorrect: the protein was human alpha-lactalbumin. $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin is the protein used to treat emphysema.
(iv) Correct: NCERT describes the milk as more balanced for human babies.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: According to NCERT, over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals belong to which group?

Cows
Mice
Fish
questions.explanation:
Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have all been produced.
However, more than 95% of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
Sheep and cows are tempting choices because of well-known examples such as Rosie the cow, but they form only a small fraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Apart from moral concerns, NCERT gives a biological reason why genetic modification of organisms needs regulation. What is that reason?
options: GM organisms always become sterile after one generation
Genetic modification can have unpredictable results when such organisms are introduced into the ecosystem
GM organisms cannot be patented, so they cannot be tracked
GM organisms always lose the introduced gene in the wild
questions.explanation:
NCERT notes that, beyond questions of morality, the biological significance of genetic modification also matters.
GM organisms can produce unpredictable results once they are introduced into the ecosystem.
This is why bodies such as GEAC are needed to assess safety.
Options (1) and (4) make absolute claims that NCERT does not support.
Option (3) is wrong because patenting of GM products is itself an issue NCERT discusses.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps of Eli Lilly's 1983 production of human insulin in the correct sequence:
P. Chains A and B are extracted.
Q. DNA sequences corresponding to chains A and B of human insulin are prepared.
R. Chains A and B are combined by creating disulphide bonds.
S. The DNA sequences are introduced into plasmids of E. coli, which produce the chains separately.
options: Q, P, S, R
S, Q, R, P
Q, S, P, R
Q, S, R, P
questions.explanation:
Step 1 (Q): two DNA sequences coding for chains A and B are prepared.
Step 2 (S): these are put into E. coli plasmids, and the bacteria make the A and B chains separately.
Step 3 (P): the separately produced chains are extracted.
Step 4 (R): the extracted chains are joined by creating disulphide bonds to form human insulin.
This approach got around the main challenge of assembling insulin into its mature form.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A child with ADA deficiency is treated by returning her own cultured lymphocytes after a functional ADA cDNA has been introduced into them with a retroviral vector. Which option correctly explains why she needs repeated treatment and identifies an approach that could give a permanent cure?
options: The retroviral vector is destroyed by her immune system; enzyme replacement therapy by injection is permanent
The engineered lymphocytes are not immortal; introducing the ADA gene isolated from marrow cells into cells at early embryonic stages
The ADA cDNA lacks a promoter and is never expressed; bone marrow transplantation is always completely curative
The ADA gene is deleted again in the lymphocytes; giving larger single doses of engineered lymphocytes
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The engineered lymphocytes are not immortal. They die over time, so periodic infusions are needed.
Step 2: NCERT states that introducing the ADA gene isolated from marrow cells into cells at early embryonic stages could be a permanent cure.
Step 3: Enzyme replacement therapy and bone marrow transplantation help some children, but NCERT says neither approach is completely curative. This rules out options 1 and 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. In biotechnology, the 'catalyst' may be a pure enzyme rather than a whole organism.
II. The Green Revolution tripled food supply and was sufficient to feed the growing human population.
III. Biotechnology involves industrial-scale production of biopharmaceuticals and biologicals using genetically modified plants and animals, not only microbes.
IV. For developing-world farmers, existing crop varieties can still give substantially higher yields through conventional breeding.
Which of the above statements are correct?
options: I and II only
I and III only
II, III and IV only
III and IV only
questions.explanation:
I. Correct. The best catalyst is an improved organism (usually a microbe) or a pure enzyme.
II. Incorrect. The Green Revolution tripled food supply, but this was still not enough for the growing population.
III. Correct. Biotechnology uses GM microbes, fungi, plants and animals.
IV. Incorrect. NCERT states further yield increases with existing varieties are not possible by conventional breeding.
Answer: (2)

(b) Alpha-1-antitrypsin
(c) Polio vaccine
(d) Alzheimer's disease

(i) Disease model
(ii) Vaccine safety testing

(iv) Biological product

(b) Alpha-1-antitrypsin is a human protein produced by transgenic animals, so it is a biological product: (iv).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Activated Bt toxin kills an insect larva by causing swelling and lysis of its midgut epithelial cells.
Reason (R): The inactive protoxin crystals are solubilised and activated by the acidic pH of the insect gut.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and creates pores. This causes the cells to swell and lyse, and the insect dies.
R is false. The crystals are solubilised and the protoxin is activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, not an acidic pH.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the RNAi strategy against Meloidogyne incognita are correct?
(i) The introduced DNA produced both sense and antisense RNA in host cells.
(ii) The sense and antisense RNAs formed a double-stranded RNA.
(iii) The dsRNA silenced a specific mRNA of the tobacco plant itself.
(iv) RNAi works by preventing translation of the target mRNA.
(v) The nematode-specific genes were introduced using Bacillus thuringiensis.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. The introduced DNA produced both sense and antisense RNA.
(ii) Correct. Being complementary, the two RNAs formed dsRNA.
(iii) Incorrect. The silenced mRNA belongs to the nematode, not the tobacco plant.
(iv) Correct. RNAi binds the mRNA and blocks its translation.
(v) Incorrect. Agrobacterium vectors were used; Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Bt toxin.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Using the NCERT definition of a Genetically Modified Organism, which of the following plants would be classified as a GMO?
options: Banana plantlets produced by micropropagation from a single explant
Virus-free sugarcane obtained by culturing apical meristem
Cotton plants expressing a cloned cry gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
A high-yielding wheat variety developed by conventional breeding during the Green Revolution
questions.explanation:
A GMO is an organism whose genes have been altered by manipulation.
Bt cotton carries a cry gene cloned from B. thuringiensis and expressed in the plant, so its genome has been deliberately changed. It is a GMO.
Micropropagated banana plantlets are somaclones, genetically identical to the parent plant.
Meristem-cultured sugarcane is simply a virus-free copy of the same plant.
Conventionally bred varieties come from crossing and selection, not gene manipulation.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding diagnostic techniques is INCORRECT?
options: ELISA detects a pathogen by amplifying its antigens to detectable levels before the antigen-antibody reaction
PCR can detect a pathogen present at very low concentration because the pathogen's nucleic acid is amplified
A radioactive probe fails to hybridise to a mutated gene because it lacks complementarity with that gene
Antigens detected in ELISA may be proteins or glycoproteins of the pathogen
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: ELISA does not amplify anything. It relies only on antigen-antibody interaction. Amplification is a feature of PCR, which acts on nucleic acids, not antigens.
(2) Correct: PCR amplifies nucleic acid, which allows early detection.
(3) Correct: The probe cannot base-pair with a mutated gene, so the mutated clone does not appear on film.
(4) Correct: NCERT lists proteins and glycoproteins as examples of antigens.
Answer: (1)

Human insulin

This made the milk nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow milk.

Human insulin is made in E. coli, and ADA is linked to gene therapy.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Statement I: Even when a plant is infected with a virus, its apical and axillary meristems are free of the virus.
Statement II: Plants raised by micropropagation from an explant are genetically identical to the parent plant and are called somaclones.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that the apical and axillary meristems stay virus-free. They can be cultured in vitro to recover healthy plants, as done in banana, sugarcane and potato.
Statement II is correct. The thousands of plants produced by micropropagation are genetically identical to the original plant, so they are somaclones.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about plant tissue culture is INCORRECT?
options: Explants are grown under sterile conditions in a special nutrient medium.
Growth regulators such as auxins and cytokinins are included in the culture medium.
Micropropagation generates wide genetic variation among the plantlets, making it a source of new varieties.
Tomato, banana and apple have been produced on a commercial scale by micropropagation.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT states that explants are grown in vitro under sterile conditions on a special nutrient medium.
(2) Correct: auxins and cytokinins are the growth regulators named for the medium.
(3) Incorrect: micropropagated plants are somaclones, genetically identical to the parent, so the method does not generate variation.
(4) Correct: NCERT names tomato, banana and apple as commercially micropropagated plants.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A child with ADA deficiency treated by introducing functional ADA cDNA into his own cultured lymphocytes requires periodic infusion of such genetically engineered lymphocytes.
Reason (R): The genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: A is true. After the functional ADA cDNA is introduced, the lymphocytes are returned to the patient, but the treatment has to be repeated periodically.
Step 2: R is true. Lymphocytes have a limited life span, so they are not immortal.
Step 3: Because the engineered cells die off, their ADA-producing population is lost over time and must be replenished. R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: In the nutrient medium used for plant tissue culture, which of the following is supplied as the carbon source?

Cytokinin
Amino acids
Sucrose
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the medium must provide a carbon source such as sucrose.
It must also provide inorganic salts, vitamins, amino acids and growth regulators.
Auxins and cytokinins are growth regulators, not carbon sources.
Amino acids are supplied as nutrients, but the carbon source named is sucrose.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the synthesis of insulin in mammals is INCORRECT?
options: Insulin is first synthesised as a pro-hormone.
The pro-hormone has to be processed before it becomes functional insulin.
The pro-hormone contains an extra stretch called the C peptide.
The C peptide is retained in mature insulin, where it joins chains A and B.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in mammals, including humans, insulin is made as a pro-hormone (pro-insulin).
(2) Correct: like a pro-enzyme, pro-insulin must be processed to become mature and functional.
(3) Correct: pro-insulin carries an extra stretch called the C peptide.
(4) Incorrect: the C peptide is removed during maturation and is absent from mature insulin. The A and B chains are joined by disulphide bridges.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Introducing the ADA gene into cells at an early embryonic stage could give a permanent cure, while introducing it into a patient's mature lymphocytes cannot. The best explanation is that:
options: Retroviral vectors cannot infect mature lymphocytes
Embryonic cells do not need the ADA enzyme, so no immune reaction occurs

The gene introduced early would be passed on to all cells arising from these cells, including those that keep producing new immune cells, whereas engineered mature lymphocytes are not immortal and die
The ADA enzyme made in the embryo is stored in the body for life
questions.explanation:
Mature engineered lymphocytes are not immortal. As they die, ADA production falls, so repeated infusions are needed.
Cells at early embryonic stages give rise to later cells, including the marrow cells that continually produce immune cells.
A functional gene placed there is inherited by all descendant cells, so ADA is made throughout life. This is a permanent cure.
Option (1) is false: retroviral vectors are exactly what is used to engineer lymphocytes.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) About 30 recombinant therapeutics have been approved for human use worldwide.
(ii) All the recombinant therapeutics approved worldwide are currently marketed in India.
(iii) Recombinant therapeutics do not induce the unwanted immunological responses common with similar products isolated from non-human sources.
(iv) Eli Lilly introduced a single DNA sequence coding for complete pro-insulin into E. coli.

(ii) Incorrect: only 12 of these are currently marketed in India.
(iii) Correct: recombinant products are identical to human proteins, so they do not provoke unwanted immune responses.
(iv) Incorrect: Eli Lilly used two separate DNA sequences, one for chain A and one for chain B.
So 2 statements are correct.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the first clinical gene therapy for adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, which vehicle was used to introduce the functional ADA cDNA into the patient's cultured lymphocytes?
options: Retroviral vector
Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Bacteriophage lambda
Plasmid of Escherichia coli
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the patient's lymphocytes are grown in culture outside the body. A functional ADA cDNA is then introduced into them using a retroviral vector.
Why it fits: retroviruses naturally insert their genetic material into animal host cells, so they make suitable vectors for human cells.
Why the others fail: the Agrobacterium Ti plasmid is a vector for plant cells. Bacteriophage lambda and E. coli plasmids are vectors for bacterial hosts, not human lymphocytes.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Bt toxin are correct?
(i) Most Bt toxins are insect-group specific, so the choice of gene depends on the crop and the target pest.
(ii) In the bacterium, the toxin exists as an inactive protoxin.
(iii) The protoxin is activated by the acidic pH of the insect gut.
(iv) The activated toxin binds to midgut epithelial cells and creates pores, causing swelling and lysis.
(v) The toxin is coded by genes named cry.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Bt toxins are largely insect-group specific.
(ii) Correct: The inactive protoxin form is why the toxin does not kill Bacillus itself.
(iii) Incorrect: Activation happens due to the alkaline pH of the insect gut, which solubilises the crystals.
(iv) Correct: Pores in midgut cells cause swelling, lysis and death of the insect.
(v) Correct: Bt toxin genes are the cry genes, e.g., cryIAc.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bt toxin crystals become active only after an insect ingests them. Which condition in the insect gut is responsible for this activation?
options: Acidic pH that denatures the crystals
Presence of bile salts that emulsify the crystals
Alkaline pH that solubilises the crystals
Low temperature that unfolds the protoxin
questions.explanation:
The Bt protein exists as an inactive protoxin within the crystals.
The insect gut has an alkaline pH. This pH solubilises the crystals and converts the protoxin into the active toxin.
An acidic pH is the tempting wrong choice. NCERT clearly links activation to the alkaline gut.
Bile salts and temperature play no role in this activation.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Insulin extracted from the pancreas of slaughtered cattle and pigs caused allergy or other reactions in some diabetic patients.
Reason (R): Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, A and B, linked together by disulphide bridges.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Animal insulin is a foreign protein and caused allergies in some patients.
R is true. Insulin is made of chains A and B joined by disulphide bridges.
However, R only describes the structure of insulin. It does not explain why animal insulin is seen as foreign; that is due to it not being identical to human insulin.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements comparing Bt cotton with RNAi-based nematode-resistant tobacco is INCORRECT?
options: Both are transgenic plants that reduce the need for chemical pesticides
In Bt cotton, the protective transgene product is a protein; in RNAi tobacco, it is a double-stranded RNA
In both cases, the protective molecule kills the pest by binding midgut epithelial cells and forming pores
In RNAi tobacco, the target of silencing is a specific mRNA of the parasite
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Both are transgenic pest-resistant crops that reduce reliance on chemical pesticides.
(2) Correct. Bt cotton expresses a Cry protein toxin, while RNAi tobacco expresses dsRNA.
(3) Incorrect. Pore formation in midgut epithelial cells applies only to activated Bt toxin; RNAi instead silences a specific nematode mRNA by blocking translation.
(4) Correct. RNAi tobacco targets a specific mRNA of the nematode.
Answer: (3)

Statement II: So far, transgenic animals have been produced only among mammals.
Choose the correct option.

Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Why is early detection of an infection generally not possible using conventional diagnostic methods such as serum and urine analysis?
options: These methods destroy the pathogen's nucleic acid during sample collection
A pathogen is usually suspected only after it has produced disease symptoms, and by then its concentration in the body is already very high
Serum and urine never contain any pathogen or its products
These methods can detect only viruses and not bacteria
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that conventional methods such as serum and urine analysis cannot detect disease early.
The presence of a pathogen is normally suspected only after it produces a disease symptom.
By that time the pathogen concentration in the body is already very high, so detection is late.
Option (1) is wrong because conventional methods do not work with nucleic acids at all.

A is false but R is true

R is false because it reverses the facts. Industrialised nations are financially rich but poor in biodiversity and traditional knowledge.
Developing and underdeveloped nations are the ones rich in biodiversity and related traditional knowledge.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct sequence after a bollworm feeds on a Bt cotton plant:
(a) Activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells
(b) Alkaline gut pH solubilises the toxin crystals and activates the protoxin
(c) Cells swell and lyse, leading to death of the insect
(d) Pores are created in the epithelial cells
(e) Insect ingests the inactive protoxin
questions.explanation:
Step 1 (e): The insect ingests the inactive protoxin.
Step 2 (b): Alkaline gut pH solubilises the crystals, giving the active toxin.
Step 3 (a): The active toxin binds to midgut epithelial cells.
Step 4 (d): The toxin creates pores in these cells.
Step 5 (c): The cells swell and lyse, and the insect dies.
The toxin cannot bind before it is activated, so option (2) is wrong.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about RNAi-based protection of tobacco against Meloidogyne incognita are correct?
(i) RNAi occurs in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.
(ii) A natural source of the complementary RNA can be infection by viruses having DNA genomes.
(iii) Transposons that replicate via an RNA intermediate can be a natural source of the complementary RNA.
(iv) In the transgenic tobacco, the specific mRNA that is silenced belongs to the host plant itself.
(v) The nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plant using Agrobacterium vectors.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: RNAi is a cellular defence that occurs in all eukaryotes.
(ii) Incorrect: the natural source is viruses with RNA genomes, not DNA genomes.
(iii) Correct: transposons that replicate via an RNA intermediate can supply the complementary RNA.
(iv) Incorrect: the silenced mRNA is the nematode's, so the parasite cannot survive in the transgenic host.
(v) Correct: Agrobacterium vectors were used to introduce the genes.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bt protoxin becomes toxic only after it is ingested by a susceptible insect.
Reason (R): The acidic pH of the insect gut solubilises the toxin crystals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The Bt protein stays as an inactive protoxin until an insect ingests it. Activation happens inside the insect's gut.
R is false. The gut pH that solubilises the crystals is alkaline, not acidic.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Transgenic tobacco plants that produce both sense and anti-sense RNA of specific nematode genes are protected from Meloidegyne incognitia.
Reason (R): The double-stranded RNA formed in the host binds to and prevents translation of the complementary mRNA of the nematode.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

R explains A: once its specific mRNA is silenced, the parasite cannot survive in the transgenic host.

Transgenic rabbits and cows have been produced, although they form a small fraction of all transgenic animals.

questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Bt toxin are correct?

Three
Four
Five

All eukaryotic organisms, as a method of cellular defence
Only animals, as part of the antibody response

questions.question: In the probe-based method for detecting a mutated gene in a clone of cells, the probe used is:

An enzyme linked to an antigen
A protein tagged with a radioactive molecule
A single-stranded DNA or RNA tagged with a radioactive molecule

A protein probe (option 3) cannot base-pair with DNA.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pro-insulin cannot act as a fully functional hormone until it has been processed.

Assertion (A): Tissue culture was developed as a technology for crop improvement because traditional breeding failed to keep pace with demand.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about transgenic animals is INCORRECT according to NCERT?

How many of the following statements are correct?

Three

questions.question: In RNA interference, a specific mRNA is silenced because
options: a complementary dsRNA molecule binds to the mRNA and prevents its translation
the gene coding for the mRNA is deleted from the chromosome
a protein toxin creates pores in the cells that make the mRNA
the mRNA is converted into DNA by reverse transcriptase
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes RNAi as silencing of a specific mRNA by a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to it and prevents its translation.
RNAi acts after transcription. The gene itself is not deleted, so option (2) is wrong.
Pore formation in gut cells describes how Bt toxin works, not RNAi.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A figure shows two sets of tobacco roots 5 days after deliberate infection with a nematode. Control roots are heavily infested, while transgenic roots are protected. Which of the following statements about the mechanism behind this protection is INCORRECT?
options: Nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plant using Agrobacterium vectors
The introduced DNA produced both sense and anti-sense RNA, which paired to form dsRNA in host cells
In nature, the complementary RNA for RNAi may come from RNA-genome viruses or from transposons that replicate via an RNA intermediate
RNAi is a defence mechanism found only in plants, and it silences genes by blocking their transcription
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Agrobacterium vectors delivered the nematode-specific genes.
(2) Correct: the sense and anti-sense RNAs are complementary, so they formed dsRNA that triggered RNAi against the nematode's specific mRNA.
(3) Correct: NCERT names RNA viruses and transposons as natural sources of the complementary RNA.
(4) Incorrect on two counts. RNAi occurs in all eukaryotic organisms, not only plants. It works by binding to the mRNA and preventing translation, not by blocking transcription.
Answer: (4)

Emphysema

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A clone library made from a patient's cells is treated with a radioactively labelled single-stranded probe complementary to the normal form of a gene and then autoradiographed. All clones appear on the film except one. What is the most valid conclusion about the clone that did not appear?
options: It carries the normal gene, because autoradiography detects only probe that has not hybridised
It has extra copies of the normal gene that used up all the probe
It produced antibodies that blocked the probe from binding
It carries a mutated form of the gene, so the probe found no complementary sequence to hybridise with
questions.explanation:
The probe hybridises only to DNA that is complementary to it, here the normal gene.
The hybridised radioactive probe is what shows up on the film. Clones with the normal gene therefore appear.
A clone with a mutated gene lacks complementarity, so the probe does not bind and the clone does not appear.
Option (1) reverses the logic: unbound probe is washed off and gives no signal.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding bio-resources and traditional knowledge is INCORRECT?
options: Traditional knowledge related to bio-resources can be used to save time, effort and expenditure during the commercialisation of modern applications
Some nations are developing laws to prevent unauthorised exploitation of their bio-resources and traditional knowledge
A company that uses a country's bio-resources after obtaining proper authorisation and paying compensation to the people concerned is committing biopiracy
There is growing realisation of injustice and inadequate compensation and benefit sharing between developed and developing countries
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT says traditional knowledge saves time, effort and expenditure during commercialisation.
(2) Correct: some nations are framing laws against unauthorised exploitation of their bio-resources.
(3) Incorrect: biopiracy means use WITHOUT proper authorisation and WITHOUT compensatory payment. Authorised, compensated use is not biopiracy.
(4) Correct: NCERT mentions growing realisation of injustice and inadequate benefit sharing between developed and developing countries.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A banana grower's elite plant has become infected by a virus. He wants thousands of virus-free plants, all with the same traits as this elite plant, within a short time. Which strategy best meets both goals?
options: Culture leaf discs from the infected plant on a medium containing sucrose, salts, vitamins and growth regulators
Fuse protoplasts of the infected banana with those of a resistant variety and regenerate somatic hybrids
Spray the infected plant with chemical pesticides and then take suckers for planting
Excise the apical meristem, culture it in vitro and then multiply the plantlets by micropropagation
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The apical meristem is virus-free even in an infected plant, so culturing it removes the virus.
Step 2: Micropropagation multiplies the plantlets rapidly, and all of them are somaclones of the elite plant.
Leaf discs may carry the virus, so option (1) fails.
Somatic hybrids would not be genetically identical to the elite plant, so option (2) fails.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Healthy plants can be recovered from virus-infected sugarcane plants by culturing their meristems in vitro.
Reason (R): The apical and axillary meristems of an infected plant remain free of the virus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT lists banana, sugarcane and potato as crops whose meristems have been cultured to obtain virus-free plants.
R is true. The apical and axillary meristems stay virus-free even in an infected plant.
R explains A, because plants grown from a virus-free meristem are themselves virus-free.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
How many of the following are application areas of biotechnology mentioned in NCERT?
(i) Therapeutics
(ii) Diagnostics
(iii) Bioremediation
(iv) Waste treatment
(v) Energy production
(vi) Catalytic cracking of petroleum fractions
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists these applications of biotechnology: therapeutics, diagnostics, GM crops for agriculture, processed food, bioremediation, waste treatment and energy production.
(i) to (v) are all on this list.
(vi) Catalytic cracking is a purely chemical process in the petroleum industry. It is not biotechnology.
So 5 items qualify.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A potato plant is infected by a virus. Which part of this plant should be cultured in vitro to recover virus-free plants?
options: Mature leaf
Apical or axillary meristem
Root cortex
Phloem tissue of the stem
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that even in a virus-infected plant, the apical and axillary meristems are free of virus.
Culturing the meristem in vitro therefore gives virus-free plants.
Mature leaves, phloem and other tissues may carry the virus, so plants raised from them would remain infected.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In plant tissue culture, an explant is any part of a plant that is taken out and grown in a test tube under sterile conditions in a special nutrient medium.
Statement II: Plants obtained by micropropagation are somaclones, i.e., they are genetically identical to the original plant from which they were grown.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT describes an explant as any plant part grown in vitro, under sterile conditions, on a special nutrient medium.
Statement II is correct. All plants raised from the same original plant by micropropagation are genetically identical to it. Such plants are called somaclones.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A researcher feeds purified Bt protoxin crystals to an insect species that is normally susceptible. A mutant line of this species has a strongly acidic midgut, while its midgut cells are otherwise normal. What is the most likely outcome for the mutant line?
options: The insects die faster because acid activates the toxin more efficiently
The insects survive because the crystals are not solubilised and the protoxin stays inactive
The insects die because the toxin directly digests their gut wall regardless of pH
The insects survive because acidic pH converts the toxin into a protein that kills Bacillus instead
questions.explanation:
Bt protein is stored as an inactive protoxin in crystals.
Activation needs the alkaline pH of the insect gut, which solubilises the crystals.
In an acidic midgut, the crystals would not be solubilised and the protoxin would remain inactive.
Without active toxin, no pores form in the midgut cells, so there is no lysis and the insects survive.
Options (1) and (3) ignore the need for alkaline activation. Option (4) has no basis in NCERT.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about transgenic animals are correct?
(i) More than 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
(ii) Transgenic mice are being used to test the safety of polio vaccine and could replace monkeys for this purpose.
(iii) Animals used for chemical safety testing are engineered to be less sensitive to toxic substances, so that results are more reliable.
(iv) The milk of the transgenic cow Rosie was enriched with human $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin.
(v) The biological role of insulin-like growth factor has been studied by introducing genes from other species that alter its formation.
(vi) Transgenic models exist for human diseases such as cystic fibrosis and Alzheimer's.
options: Three
Five
Two
Four
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: mice make up over 95 per cent of transgenic animals.
(ii) Correct, as stated in NCERT.
(iii) Incorrect: these animals are made more sensitive to toxic substances, which gives results in less time.
(iv) Incorrect: Rosie's milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin. $\alpha$-1-antitrypsin is the protein used for emphysema.
(v) Correct.
(vi) Correct.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1983, Eli Lilly introduced DNA sequences coding for the A and B chains of human insulin into the plasmids of:
options: Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Bacillus thuringiensis
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Escherichia coli
questions.explanation:
Eli Lilly, an American company, prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin.
It introduced them into plasmids of E. coli, which then produced the insulin chains.
Agrobacterium is the vector used in NCERT's RNAi example for nematode resistance, not in insulin production.
Yeast is a eukaryote, and it was not the host used here.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bt toxin protein causes death of a lepidopteran larva only after the larva has ingested it.
Reason (R): The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the toxin crystals and converts the inactive protoxin into an active toxin, which creates pores in midgut epithelial cells.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the toxin exists as an inactive protoxin, so it becomes harmful only after it is ingested.
R is true: alkaline gut pH solubilises the crystals and activates the toxin.
The active toxin binds the surface of midgut epithelial cells and makes pores, causing swelling, lysis and death of the insect.
R therefore explains why ingestion is required for the toxin to act.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Recombinant therapeutics do not induce unwanted immunological responses in human patients.
Reason (R): Recombinant therapeutics such as human insulin made in bacteria are identical to the natural human proteins.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation:
A is true: unlike products isolated from non-human sources, recombinant therapeutics do not cause unwanted immune responses.
R is true: human insulin made in bacteria has a structure absolutely identical to the natural molecule.
The body does not treat a protein identical to its own as foreign. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: ADA deficiency is caused by:
options: Deletion of the gene for adenosine deaminase
Excess production of adenosine deaminase
A viral infection of lymphocytes
Deletion of the gene for insulin-like growth factor
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that ADA deficiency is caused by deletion of the gene for adenosine deaminase.
Because the gene is missing, the enzyme is not made, and the immune system cannot function properly.
It is a hereditary gene defect, not an infection and not an excess of the enzyme.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): To protect tobacco from nematodes, the nematode-specific DNA was introduced into the host in such a way that it produced both sense and antisense RNA in host cells.
Reason (R): Sense and antisense RNAs are complementary to each other, so together they form double-stranded RNA that initiates RNAi.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The introduced DNA was designed to produce both sense and antisense RNA in the host cells.
R is true. These two RNAs are complementary, so they pair to form dsRNA, and this dsRNA triggers RNAi.
R correctly explains A, because dsRNA can form only when both strands are made. Producing both strands is exactly why the DNA was designed this way.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Golden rice is a genetically modified crop developed to improve the nutritional value of food.
Reason (R): Golden rice has been engineered mainly to resist insect pests and reduce pesticide use.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT gives golden rice (Vitamin A enriched rice) as its example of enhanced nutritional value of food.
R is false. Golden rice is not a pest-resistant crop.
NCERT's examples of pest-resistant crops are Bt crops such as Bt cotton, which carry Bt toxin genes.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: ELISA detects infection by a pathogen. On which principle does it work?
options: Amplification of the pathogen's nucleic acid
Antigen-antibody interaction
Hybridisation of a radioactive probe with complementary DNA
Silencing of a specific mRNA by dsRNA
questions.explanation:
ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immuno-sorbent Assay) works on antigen-antibody interaction.
It detects either the pathogen's antigens (proteins, glycoproteins) or the antibodies made against the pathogen.
Amplifying nucleic acid describes PCR, which is the most tempting wrong option.
Probe hybridisation is followed by autoradiography, and dsRNA silencing describes RNAi.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the Basmati rice patent case are correct?
(i) 27 documented varieties of Basmati are grown in India.
(ii) The 'new' variety was obtained by crossing Indian Basmati with tall, high-yielding varieties.
(iii) Basmati finds mention in ancient texts, folklore and poetry.
(iv) The patent allowed the company to sell the 'new' variety in the US and abroad.
(v) The 'new' variety was derived from varieties originally developed by the American company itself.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT states that 27 documented Basmati varieties are grown in India.
(ii) Incorrect: Indian Basmati was crossed with semi-dwarf varieties, not tall ones.
(iii) Correct: Basmati is referred to in ancient texts, folklore and poetry.
(iv) Correct: the patent let the company sell the 'new' Basmati in the US and abroad.
(v) Incorrect: the variety was actually derived from Indian farmers' varieties.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The 1997 Basmati patent could restrict other people selling Basmati rice, and not merely those selling the exact 'new' variety.
Reason (R): The patent extended to functional equivalents of the claimed variety.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true: NCERT states that the Basmati patent extended to functional equivalents.
A is true: because the patent covered functional equivalents, other people selling Basmati rice could also be restricted by it.
This wide scope is why the patent threatened traditional Basmati sellers, even though the 'new' variety had itself been derived from Indian farmers' varieties.
R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are benefits of genetically modified crops as listed in NCERT?
(i) Tolerance to cold, drought, salt and heat
(ii) Reduced reliance on chemical pesticides
(iii) Increased requirement of chemical fertilisers
(iv) Enhanced nutritional value of food
(v) Faster exhaustion of soil fertility
(vi) Reduced post-harvest losses
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: GM crops tolerate abiotic stresses.
(ii) Correct: pest-resistant crops reduce the use of chemical pesticides.
(iii) Incorrect: GM crops use minerals more efficiently, so the need for fertilisers is not increased.
(iv) Correct: golden rice is an example of enhanced nutritional value.
(v) Incorrect: GM crops prevent early exhaustion of soil fertility.
(vi) Correct: GM has helped reduce post-harvest losses.
This gives four correct statements.
Answer: (3)

How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
(ii) The milk of the transgenic cow Rosie contained human alpha-1-antitrypsin.
(iii) The 'new' Basmati patented in the US in 1997 was derived by crossing Indian Basmati with semi-dwarf varieties.

questions.question:
Statement I: Bt crops act as bio-pesticides, so they reduce the need to spray chemical insecticides.
Statement II: Bt toxin crystals become active only in the acidic environment of the insect gut.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The Bt toxin gene expressed in plants gives resistance to insects without insecticides. In effect, the plant becomes a bio-pesticide.
Statement II is incorrect. The insect gut has an alkaline pH, not an acidic one.
The alkaline pH solubilises the crystals and converts the inactive protoxin into the active toxin.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Enzyme replacement therapy completely cures adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
Reason (R): In enzyme replacement therapy, functional ADA is given to the patient by injection.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true. In enzyme replacement therapy, functional ADA is injected into the patient.
A is false. NCERT notes that neither bone marrow transplantation nor enzyme replacement therapy is completely curative.
Only introducing the ADA gene into cells at early embryonic stages could be a permanent cure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose a lepidopteran larva is experimentally treated so that its gut contents stay acidic instead of alkaline. It is then fed leaves of a Bt cotton plant. What is the most likely outcome?
options: The larva dies faster, because acid speeds up conversion of the protoxin to toxin
The toxin is activated but cannot bind to midgut cells, so the larva survives
The crystals are not solubilised and the protoxin stays inactive, so the midgut cells are not lysed
The toxin is digested and then kills the Bacillus present in the larval gut
questions.explanation:
Bt toxin is ingested as inactive protoxin crystals.
The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilises the crystals and converts the protoxin into the active toxin.
If the gut is acidic, this conversion does not happen, so no active toxin binds to the midgut epithelium.
No pores form, so the cells do not swell or lyse, and the larva survives.
Option 2 fails because the toxin would not be activated in the first place.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Agro-chemical based agriculture
(B) Organic agriculture
(C) Genetically engineered crop-based agriculture
(D) Downstream processing
List-II
(i) Purifying a recombinant protein from a fermentation broth

A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(i)
A-(i), B-(iv), C-(iii), D-(ii)

B-(iv): Organic agriculture avoids synthetic chemicals and uses natural inputs.

questions.question:
Statement I: Every plant obtained by micropropagation is genetically identical to the original plant from which it was grown.
Statement II: Scientists discovered during the 1970s that whole plants could be regenerated from explants.
Choose the correct option:

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

A. C peptide
B. Disulphide bridges
C. Plasmids of E. coli
D. Pancreas of cattle and pigs
List-II:
(i) Earlier source of insulin that caused allergy in some patients
(ii) Removed during maturation of pro-insulin
(iii) Link chain A with chain B of insulin
(iv) Used by Eli Lilly to produce insulin chains
options: A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(i)

A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(ii), D-(i)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A figure compares two sets of tobacco roots. Roots of a control plant are heavily infested by nematodes. Roots of a transgenic plant, 5 days after deliberate nematode infection, look healthy. Which statement correctly explains the protection seen in the transgenic plant?
options: The transgenic roots secrete Cry protein that is activated in the alkaline gut of the nematode
The transgenic plant makes dsRNA complementary to a nematode mRNA, so that mRNA is not translated in the parasite
The transgenic plant lacks the receptor through which the nematode enters the roots
The transgenic plant produces antibodies that bind antigens on the nematode surface
questions.explanation:
This is Figure 10.2: host plant-generated dsRNA protects the roots against nematode infestation.
The transgene produces sense and antisense RNA, which pair into dsRNA complementary to a specific nematode mRNA.
When the nematode feeds, that mRNA is silenced and not translated, so the parasite cannot survive.
Option (1) describes the Bt mechanism used against insects, and plants do not make antibodies.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

Hemipterans

questions.question:
Match List-I (benefit of genetic modification) with List-II (description/example):
List-I
(A) Abiotic stress tolerance

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the disorder treated in the first clinical gene therapy, is caused by deletion of the gene for adenosine deaminase.
Statement II: Lymphocytes given a functional ADA cDNA provide a permanent cure, because these engineered lymphocytes are immortal.
Choose the correct option.

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. ADA deficiency results from deletion of the ADA gene. The first clinical gene therapy for it was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ability of a single plant cell or explant to regenerate into a complete plant when cultured in a suitable medium is termed:
options: Somatic hybridisation
Totipotency
Micropropagation
Somaclonal variation
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines totipotency as the capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell or explant.
This property is what makes plant tissue culture possible.
Micropropagation is the method that uses this property to produce thousands of plants. It is not the property itself.
Somatic hybridisation is the fusion of protoplasts from two different plants.
Somaclonal variation is not the ability to regenerate a whole plant.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: RNA interference occurs in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. In RNAi, a complementary dsRNA silences a specific mRNA by preventing its translation.
Statement II: To protect tobacco against Meloidegyne incognitia, the nematode-specific genes introduced through Agrobacterium vectors produced only anti-sense RNA in the host cells.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT describes RNAi as a defence mechanism found in all eukaryotes, in which a complementary dsRNA blocks translation of a specific mRNA.
Statement II is incorrect. The introduced DNA produced both sense and anti-sense RNA. These paired to form dsRNA, which triggered RNAi and silenced the nematode's mRNA.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The insecticidal protein produced in Bt cotton plants is coded by a gene taken from which organism?
options: Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Bacillus thuringiensis
Meloidogyne incognita
Escherichia coli
questions.explanation:
Bt toxin is made by the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. 'Bt' is short for this name.
The Bt toxin gene was cloned from this bacterium and expressed in crop plants. This gave the plants a built-in bio-pesticide.
Agrobacterium is used as a vector for gene transfer. It is not the source of the toxin gene.
Meloidogyne incognita is a nematode pest. E. coli is the host used for insulin production.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Which of the following statements about plant tissue culture is INCORRECT?
options: Scientists learnt during the 1950s that whole plants could be regenerated from explants
Tomato, banana and apple have been produced on a commercial scale by micropropagation
Micropropagation allows a large number of plants to be propagated in a very short time
Plants raised from a single parent plant by micropropagation show wide genetic variation, which helps in selecting new varieties
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: regeneration of whole plants from explants was discovered in the 1950s.
(2) Correct: NCERT names tomato, banana and apple as crops micropropagated commercially.
(3) Correct: rapid, large-scale propagation is the main advantage of micropropagation.
(4) Incorrect: micropropagated plants are somaclones. They are genetically identical to the parent, so they do not provide variation for selecting new varieties.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 · Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: PCR can detect a bacterial or viral infection even before disease symptoms appear in the patient.
Statement II: ELISA can detect an infection only by identifying the pathogen's nucleic acid, not its proteins or the host's antibodies.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. PCR amplifies the pathogen's nucleic acid, so very low concentrations of a bacterium or virus can be detected before symptoms appear. It is used routinely to detect HIV.
Statement II is incorrect. ELISA works on antigen-antibody interaction. It detects an infection either through pathogen antigens (proteins, glycoproteins) or through antibodies made against the pathogen. It does not detect nucleic acid.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1983, Eli Lilly produced the polypeptide chains of human insulin using recombinant DNA technology. Which host organism carried the plasmids with the DNA sequences for these chains?
options: Agrobacterium tumefaciens
Escherichia coli
Bacillus thuringiensis
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
questions.explanation:
In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences, one for chain A and one for chain B of human insulin.
Both sequences were introduced into plasmids of E. coli, which then produced the insulin chains.
Agrobacterium is a vector used for plants, such as in the RNAi nematode-resistance work.
B. thuringiensis is the source of Bt toxin and was not used to make insulin.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which technique is now routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients by amplifying very small amounts of the virus's nucleic acid?
options: Autoradiography
Gel electrophoresis
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
Micro-propagation
questions.explanation:
PCR amplifies nucleic acid, so even a very low concentration of a virus can be detected.
NCERT notes that PCR is routinely used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients.
Autoradiography only detects a radioactive probe on film. It does not amplify anything.
Answer: (3)

Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) cryIAb

List-II

(IV) Protein controls cotton bollworms
Choose the correct answer.

A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

B-IV: the proteins coded by cryIAc (and cryIIAb) control cotton bollworms.
C-I: Meloidegyne incognitia is a nematode that infects tobacco roots and greatly reduces yield.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Bt crops are correct?
(i) The Bt toxin gene is cloned from a bacterium and expressed in plants, creating a bio-pesticide.
(ii) B. thuringiensis forms toxin crystals continuously throughout all phases of its growth.
(iii) Most Bt toxins are insect-group specific, so the gene chosen depends on the crop and the targeted pest.
(iv) The activated toxin acts on midgut epithelial cells of the insect.
(v) The protein encoded by cryIAb controls cotton bollworms.
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: The plant itself makes the insecticidal protein.
(ii) Incorrect: The crystals form only during a particular phase of growth.
(iii) Correct: NCERT states that the choice of gene depends on the crop and the target pest.
(iv) Correct: The activated toxin binds midgut epithelium and creates pores.
(v) Incorrect: cryIAb controls the corn borer. Cotton bollworms are controlled by cryIAc and cryIIAb.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about plant tissue culture are correct?
(i) The nutrient medium must provide a carbon source such as sucrose.
(ii) Plants obtained by micro-propagation are somaclones, genetically identical to the original plant.
(iii) The apical and axillary meristems of a virus-infected plant are free of virus.
(iv) Totipotency is the capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell or explant.
(v) Growth regulators such as auxins and cytokinins are not required in the medium.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the medium must contain a carbon source like sucrose.
(ii) Correct: plants produced by micro-propagation are somaclones.
(iii) Correct: this is why meristem culture gives virus-free plants.
(iv) Correct: this is the NCERT definition of totipotency.
(v) Incorrect: growth regulators such as auxins and cytokinins are essential, along with inorganic salts, vitamins and amino acids.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: GM crops have been made more tolerant to abiotic stresses. Which of the following is NOT an abiotic stress?
options: Drought
High salt concentration in soil
Attack by insect pests
Cold
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists the abiotic stresses as cold, drought, salt and heat. These are non-living environmental factors.
An insect pest is a living organism, so its attack is a biotic stress.
NCERT deals with pests under a separate benefit: reduced reliance on chemical pesticides through pest-resistant crops.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: ELISA can detect an infection either by the presence of antigens of the pathogen or by the presence of antibodies synthesised against the pathogen.
Statement II: PCR detects a pathogen at low concentration by amplifying its proteins and glycoproteins.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. ELISA can detect either the pathogen's antigens (proteins, glycoproteins) or the antibodies made against the pathogen.
Statement II is incorrect. PCR amplifies nucleic acid (DNA), not proteins or glycoproteins.
Proteins and glycoproteins are the antigens detected in ELISA.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Milk from the transgenic cow Rosie was nutritionally a more balanced product for human babies than natural cow milk.
Reason (R): Rosie's milk was enriched with human alpha-1-antitrypsin.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

A is true: NCERT states that Rosie's milk was nutritionally more balanced for human babies than natural cow milk.
R is false: the milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin, at 2.4 grams per litre.
Alpha-1-antitrypsin is a different human protein, used to treat emphysema.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Structurally, a mature human insulin molecule consists of:
options: a single long polypeptide chain folded by hydrogen bonds
two short polypeptide chains, A and B
three polypeptide chains, A, B and C
four identical polypeptide subunits
questions.explanation:
According to NCERT, insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, chain A and chain B.
The C peptide is present only in pro-insulin. It is removed during maturation, so mature insulin does not have three chains.
Insulin is not a single chain, and it does not have four subunits.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Meloidogyne incognita
(B) Agrobacterium

(D) Transposon
List-II
(I) Mobile genetic element replicating via an RNA intermediate
(II) Nematode parasite of tobacco roots
(III) Vector used to transfer nematode-specific genes
(IV) Forms dsRNA that initiates RNAi
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

B-III: Agrobacterium vectors carried the nematode-specific genes into the plant.

D-I: Transposons are mobile genetic elements that replicate via an RNA intermediate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A patient treated with genetically engineered lymphocytes carrying functional ADA cDNA requires periodic infusion of such lymphocytes.
Reason (R): Lymphocytes are not immortal cells.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that the patient needs periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes.
R is true: these lymphocytes are not immortal, so they die off over time.
R explains A: as the engineered cells die, the ADA they produce is lost, so fresh engineered cells must be infused again.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In industrial biotechnology, the term 'downstream processing' refers to:
options: Selecting an improved microbe to act as the catalyst
Maintaining optimal temperature and pH for the catalyst inside the reactor
Purifying the protein or organic compound after it has been produced
Introducing the desired gene into the host organism
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes downstream processing as the technologies used to purify the protein or organic compound formed.
Selecting an improved microbe is the 'best catalyst' research area.
Maintaining reactor conditions is the 'optimal conditions through engineering' research area.
Gene introduction is a step of rDNA technology, not purification.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the gene therapy for ADA deficiency, which type of vector is used to introduce the functional ADA cDNA into the patient's lymphocytes?
options: Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium
pBR322 plasmid of E. coli
Retroviral vector
Bacteriophage lambda vector
questions.explanation:
NCERT: a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into cultured lymphocytes using a retroviral vector.
This fits the summary, which says viruses that introduce their genetic material into host cells are used as vectors in gene therapy.
The Ti plasmid is the tempting option, but it is used for plants (Agrobacterium), not human lymphocytes.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have all been produced. Which animal makes up more than 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals?
options: Sheep
Cows
Mice
Fish

NCERT states that over 95 per cent of all existing transgenic animals are mice.
Mice are also the animals being developed to test vaccine safety, for example for the polio vaccine.
Cows (for example Rosie) and sheep have been made transgenic, but only in small numbers.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, a genetic defect is corrected in gene therapy by:
options: Removing the defective chromosome from all body cells
Delivering a normal gene into the individual or embryo to take over the function of the non-functional gene
Injecting the missing enzyme regularly into the blood
Transplanting the entire organ that shows the defect
questions.explanation:
Gene therapy inserts genes into a person's cells and tissues to treat a disease.
A normal gene is delivered into the individual or embryo so that it takes over the function of, and compensates for, the non-functional gene.
Injecting the enzyme is enzyme replacement therapy. That is a different, non-curative approach.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) C peptide
(b) Disulphide bridges
(c) Pro-hormone
(d) Insulin from cattle and pig pancreas
List-II
(i) Hold chains A and B together
(ii) Removed during maturation of insulin
(iii) Caused allergy in some patients
(iv) Precursor that must be processed to become functional
Choose the correct option:

a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii
a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i

questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The capacity of any plant cell or explant to regenerate into a whole plant is called totipotency.
Statement II: Plants produced by micro-propagation are somaclones, genetically identical to the plant from which they were grown.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT defines totipotency as the capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell or explant.
Statement II is correct. Micro-propagation produces thousands of plants from one parent by tissue culture, so all of them carry the parent's genotype. They are therefore called somaclones.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In India, which body was set up by the Government to decide whether GM research is valid and whether it is safe to introduce GM organisms for public services?
options: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC)
questions.explanation:
Genetic modification can have unpredictable results when GM organisms are released into an ecosystem, so regulation is needed.
The Indian Government set up GEAC to decide on the validity of GM research and the safety of releasing GM organisms for public use.
ICAR, ICMR and CSIR are research councils. NCERT does not name them as the GM approval authority.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Bt toxin protein crystals formed by Bacillus thuringiensis do not kill the bacterium itself.
Reason (R): The Bt protoxin is converted into its active form by the acidic pH of the insect gut.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Inside the bacterium, the toxin exists as an inactive protoxin, so it does not harm B. thuringiensis.
R is false. The crystals are solubilised and the toxin is activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, not an acidic pH.
After activation, the toxin binds to midgut epithelial cells and makes pores, which cause swelling, lysis and death of the insect.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: After activation in the insect gut, the Bt toxin binds to which cells to bring about the death of the insect?
options: Salivary gland cells
Malpighian tubule cells
Midgut epithelial cells
Nerve cells of the ventral nerve cord
questions.explanation:
The activated Bt toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells.
It creates pores in these cells, which causes them to swell and lyse.
This damage eventually kills the insect.
The toxin does not act on nerves, salivary glands or excretory tubules.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The two polypeptide chains, A and B, of mature human insulin are held together by:
options: Peptide bonds
Hydrogen bonds only
Disulphide bridges
Phosphodiester bonds
questions.explanation:
Insulin consists of two short polypeptide chains, A and B.
These chains are linked to each other by disulphide bridges.
Peptide bonds join the amino acids within each chain. They do not link the two chains to each other.
Phosphodiester bonds occur in nucleic acids, not in proteins.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, there is growing public anger about patents in biotechnology mainly because:
options: patents are granted only to Indian companies, which excludes foreign researchers

companies are being granted patents for products and technologies that use genetic materials, plants and other biological resources long identified, developed and used by farmers and indigenous people
patented GM crops have been proved to cause cancer in humans
patents prevent the government from setting up regulatory bodies like GEAC
questions.explanation:
NCERT says the anger arises because some companies obtain patents on products and technologies that use genetic materials, plants and other bio-resources.
These resources have long been identified, developed and used by farmers and indigenous people of a particular region or country.
Option (2) matches this exactly.
NCERT makes no claim that GM crops cause cancer.
Patents also do not stop the government from setting up GEAC.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) PCR
(B) ELISA
(C) Radioactive single-stranded DNA/RNA probe
(D) Transgenic mice
List-II
(I) Antigen-antibody interaction
(II) Testing the safety of polio vaccine
(III) Detecting very low concentrations of a pathogen, e.g., HIV, by amplifying its nucleic acid
(IV) The clone carrying a mutated gene does not appear on the photographic film
Choose the correct answer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transgenic animals have been used to produce human alpha-1-antitrypsin. This protein is used in the treatment of:
options: Emphysema
Phenylketonuria
Adenosine deaminase deficiency
Rheumatoid arthritis
questions.explanation:
NCERT cites human alpha-1-antitrypsin as a biological product made by transgenic animals. It is used to treat emphysema.
Phenylketonuria is mentioned separately, only as a disease for which similar attempts are being made.
ADA deficiency is treated by gene therapy or enzyme replacement.
Rheumatoid arthritis appears in the chapter only as a disease model.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants produced through micropropagation are genetically identical to the plant from which they were raised. Such plants are termed:
options: Somatic hybrids
Transgenic plants
Somaclones
Polyploids
questions.explanation:
Micropropagation produces many plants from tissue of a single parent plant.
Each of these plants is genetically identical to the original plant. NCERT calls them somaclones.
Somatic hybrids come from fusing protoplasts of two different varieties, so they are not identical to either parent.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The particular Bt toxin gene introduced into a crop is chosen according to the crop and the pest to be controlled.
Reason (R): Most Bt toxins are specific to a particular group of insects.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that the choice of genes depends on the crop and the targeted pest. For example, cryIAc and cryIIAb are used against cotton bollworms, while cryIAb is used against corn borer.
R is true. Most Bt toxins are insect-group specific.
R explains A: a toxin kills only certain insect groups, so the gene must match the pest of that crop.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Human insulin produced by Eli Lilly's 1983 method lacks the C peptide.
Statement II: In Eli Lilly's method, chains A and B were joined by disulphide bonds inside the E. coli cell, so the bacterium released fully mature insulin.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Only the DNA sequences for chains A and B were used. No C peptide was ever made, so the final insulin has none.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT says the chains were produced separately, then extracted and combined by creating disulphide bonds outside the bacteria.
The main difficulty was assembling insulin into its mature form. Making the chains separately and joining them afterwards solved this problem.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Thousands of banana plants are raised by micropropagation from a single explant of one elite plant. These plants are called somaclones because they are:
options: Hybrids formed by fusing protoplasts of two banana varieties
Genetically identical to the original plant from which the explant was taken
Genetically varied plants arising from mutations in the culture medium
Transgenic plants carrying a foreign gene introduced by Agrobacterium
questions.explanation:
Micropropagation regenerates whole plants from an explant using totipotency.
These plants arise from the parent's own cells by mitotic growth, so they are genetically identical to it. NCERT calls them somaclones.
Protoplast fusion gives somatic hybrids, not somaclones.
Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer gives transgenic plants, not somaclones.
Answer: (2)
